  • center

questions.question: What is secondary data? Elaborate the sources of secondary data along with its merits and demerits. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Secondary data refers to data that has already been collected, processed,
  • and published by someone else for a purpose different from the current
  • research. Instead of gathering fresh (primary) data, researchers use
  • existing information available in reports, publications, or databases.
  • Secondary data can be broadly classified into pub lished and unpublished
  • sources:
  • Published Sources :
  • o Government Publications: Census reports, Economic Surveys,
  • Statistical Abstracts, reports from ministries and departments.
  • o International Organizations: Reports from organizations like World
  • Bank, International Monetary Fund, United Nations.
  • o Research Institutions and Universities: Academic journals, working
  • papers, theses, and dissertations.
  • o Books, Journals, Newspapers, and M agazines: Provide qualitative
  • and quantitative information.
  • o Websites and Online Databases: Government portals, company
  • websites, and digital archives.
